Lower back pain caused by sitting with a wallet or phone in your back pocket 💥 🤯 Our pelvis is the base of support for the body, if that is shifted or out of line, it can cause dysfunction in everything above and below We should sit with the weight distributed evenly between our two sit bones. If you have a phone or wallet in one pocket, it shifts the weight and causes a massive change in angle in the pelvis. This will then lead to lower back and hip flexor tightness and a strain on the Sacro-iliac joint This can cause shoulder and neck pain due to the shift in forces Please remove the wallet!!! The joy in life as a zebra with chronic pain 🥴 Everyday for three years I've had a burning sensation run through my toes sporadically, slowly advancing to other parts of my feet. It's been rather debilitating at times, it's like my toes experience period cramps! 😂 but the doctors have done their usual tests and ruled out rheumatoid arthritis, mortem neuroma and bunions being the cause which just left me still in the dark about my health. So today I went to the hospital, again, and the doctor did yet another physical exam. Like his predecessors he couldn't see anything wrong with me, he did compliment my flexibility though 😅 (hypermobile joints) and so a new path has been set out. More X-Rays, MRIs, physical therapy? who knows at this point what's to come but he did make sure to tell me that after this long, without any physical traits to go off of, the cause of my pain might just have to remain a mystery. A Functional Medicine approach to arthritis –  Another common concern I see in my practice is arthritis.  By the time a patient sees me they may already be that bad that a hip (or other) replacement is on the cards.  BUT – if you catch it early and ideally yet, aim to prevent it from happening in the first place, Functional Medicine and Precision Health Optimisation can be a great way to support you along that journey.  A few factors that can contribute to arthritis are  Chronic low-grade inflammation and free radical damage, often due to  👉 Lingering infections such as gut bacteria imbalances, candida albicans, viruses, parasites,  👉 Hidden food intolerances,  👉 Heavy metals accumulation such as mercury and lead.  Furthermore, we like to test for nutrient levels like omega 3, zinc, vitamin D, that are important support the immune system, lower inflammation, but also avoid it from overreacting (new research suggests there may be an autoimmune component even to osteoarthritis, and in large part an inflammatory process, which used to be thought of as a mostly a ‘wear and tear’ condition).  As always: test, don’t guess. And prevention is better than treating once the body has already gone down far the wrong path.  Do you have a condition you'd like addressed? Book a 1-on-1 consultation in which we take a deep dive into your history, concerns, goals, and decide on testing to get to the root of your concerns.  Once test results are back, we then come up with a very bespoke strategy to address and remove those triggers, so that the body can do its thing and heal (as best as possible). MCL - Medial collateral ligament  Media collateral ligament sprains are the most common knee injury.  The MCL is a ligament on the inside of the knee that acts as a stabiliser to prevent valgus stress ( knee caving in ) and rotational forces.  A common cause of a MCL injury is a valgus stress on a stationary knee or sudden forceful turning twisting and cutting.  Signs and Symptoms  * knee giving out * Fluid and blood filling the joint ( severe case) * Painful to touch MCL * MOI - mechanism of injury  Grade 1 tear = no instability of the knee, tenderness on the MCL , few fibres torn. Grade 2 tear = More superficial fibres torn, pain on palpating MCL, tender with no instability.  Grade 3 tear = Complete tear, unstable  Treatment of grade 1-2 * Early rehabilitation  * Weight bearing when pain reduced  * Immobilisation leads to weaker ligaments  * Progressive strength of on hams and quads.  * Favourable long term outcomes  Grade 3 tears are often more complicated and can occur with other ligaments, ACL, PCL and Meniscus, often requiring surgery.  #medialcollateralligamentinjury #PCL #meniscus #injuryrecovery #injuryprevention #physicaltherapy #musculoskeletal #sportrehabilitation #returntoplay

Cervical Radiculopathy (CR) otherwise known as a Pinched cervical nerve   This condition is caused by a compressed cervical spine nerve root.  Symptoms of CR is Pain that radiates down the arm from the neck along the course of the nerve. You may also experience muscle weakness and impaired tendon flexors.  Most frequently caused by disc trauma / herniation and commonly affects younger people in the 3rd and 4th decade.  Disc degeneration increases with age and people in the 5th and 6th decades are affected.  People in the 7th decade of life are likely to  experience CR due to spinal narrowing as a result of cartilage changes.  Treatment of CR -  85% are said to resolve in 8-12 weeks.  Physical therapy consists of gentle ROM exercises, Acupuncture to treat trigger points and ease inflammation, cervical traction and neurodynamics .  When pain is reduced you can work on posture and muscle imbalances with progressive exercises. As we age, the levels of collagen in our bodies decline. This is due to a number of factors, and things like menopause can cause it to accelerate further. This results in many of the physical signs of ageing.  Our skin wrinkles and sags, our joints ache and our bone mass decreases. We look and feel older and become more prone to harmful conditions like osteoarthritis or osteoporosis. With less collagen, our physical wellness decreases. This can also take a toll on our mental wellbeing as confidence wanes and physical discomfort persists. Over pronation  In 2020 I was having so many issues with my joints especially my knees and in the August that year I started seeing a musculoskeletal physio and I’ve been there ever since. CC:  “I am not typing this. I am saying this. I want you to hear the breath passing through my vocal cords and the air in front of my lips vibrating with the sounds of my words. I want you to feel those vibrations hitting your eardrums and sending these messages to your brain: I am speaking this because I can’t type it. I am using my voice because I can’t use my hands. I am louder because I am less able to write my message down. When I type, each repetitive motion stokes a fire in my knuckles until tears pool along the base of my lower eyelid and gently fall down my flushed, swollen face. I am stronger because I am weaker. I am weaker because I am at battle with every breath I take. I am louder out of necessity; my words are my warcry. I scream my message because I can’t get up, walk over to you, and whisper it calmly into your ear.  I am forced to rest, and if my body can’t reach where I want to go, my voice will crescendo until my words reach the destination. I will project my voice to where my body cannot take me until my lungs melts and my diaphragm seizes. And when my words falter, for I have lost yet another means of being human, I will whisper into this stupid fucking notes app and watch my words transform into visuals that can go anywhere. That can go to all of the places that I cannot, and yet in a way take me along with them. my energy will always flow, and as the channels through which they travel drop off one by one as disease conquers me, the current will flow ever stronger from what channel is left. In that way, perhaps I am louder, stronger, and more powerful than ever before.” “Louder, Stronger, & More Powerful Than Ever Before.” Poem about new symptoms and coming to terms with the various facets of disability. ❤️‍🩹 #poetry #poem #poetryreading #spokenword #spokenwordpoetry #endo #disabled #endometriosis #chronicillness #jointpain #autoimmune #autoimmunedisease #chronicpain #spoonie #chronicallyill #chronicfatigue #chronicpainwarrior #chronicillnesswarrior #zebrastrong #endostrong #chronicpainawareness #chronicillnessawareness #spoonielife #spooniewarrior #warrior #acceptance #healthcare #pelvicpain

Snap, crackle & Pop… We’ve all experienced those noises at some point in our lives. Crepitus is when there is a sensation or noise when you move a joint which can be described as clicking, cracking, creaking, crunching, grating or popping. You can experience crepitus at ANY age & it can affect any joint in the body.  It’s most commonly found in your knees, hands, feet, lower back, hips or shoulders. (So most joints). There are a few causes for crepitus but the most common ones are; 1. Bubbles of air popping inside your joint. Which is the noise you’ll hear if you crack your knuckles & is usually painless. This actually does have a name, it’s called cavitation. 2. Your bones rubbing against each other, usually caused by arthritis – often with chronic pain or discomfort. 3. Snapping of tendons or ligaments over the bony surfaces of your joint which can also sometimes be painful. In most cases you won’t need to have treatment for crepitus, your joints can crack or pop from time to time.  Applying ice to the joint & taking non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs is usually enough to alleviate the pain & inflammation.  However, if you’re experiencing crepitus with pain, swelling or discomfort, it’s probably best to go see your GP. Arthritis means inflammation or swelling of one or more joints, and is a term used to describe over 100 conditions that affect joints, connective tissue and tissues around the joints. Arthritis affects around 10 million people in the uk.  Symptoms include pain, tenderness and stiffness of joints, joint inflammation, restricted movement, warm reddening of the skin over affected joints, muscle weakness and muscle wastage.  Red Light and Near Red Light Therapy are known to help manage symptoms of arthritis by; •decreasing pain •modulating inflammation (decreasing pro inflammatory cytokines) and increasing anti inflammatory cytokines.  •increasing circulation to the area •stimulating wound healing and cellular repair mechanisms in the damaged joint.  A group of researchers in Taiwan, found that red light therapy reduced joint pain by 70% in rheumatoid arthritis sufferers compared to a placebo group. In addition, they also saw reduction in morning stiffness and increased flexibility.  Whilst a study conducted on 50 patients with osteoarthritis found that frequent red and near red Light Therapy treatments reduced osteoarthritis knee pain by 50%. Why Mobility > Flexibility There are two main reasons why you want to train Mobility and not just Flexibility  1. Flexibility is a passive range of motion (ROM). ● Your body can be there but it can't control that ROM. ● A range without control is predisposed to injury. ● Your Brain will decrease your Flexibility to reduce the risk of injury. ●Continually stretching to maintain it can be detrimental to your body over time. As connective tissue (fascia) weakens and your body has to compensate by making other areas hold more tension AND potential end up with joint pain and degeneration form this. 2. Mobility is an active range of motion. ● Strength allows you to actually use that ROM. ● Your Body feels safe moving through your ROM and doesn't need to tighten up to prevent potential injury. ● Rather than constantly spending time and energy to regain your ROM, you can progressively build your strength in your ROM. ●Mobility gives your body better options to move with. At IBA we teach a simple yet comprehensive method to improve and maintain your mobility for life. As you'll recognise from my other posts, this is all connected physically, mentally and emotionally. “Listen to your body” works both ways. We do need to honour pain and pull back from intense exercises that may induce or exacerbate that pain… But  We also need to keep moving in ways that prevent pain, stiffness or general aches in the long run. This is usually low level, everyday movement that is diverse and fun.  Many of us spend our day locked in just a few positions and then conduct a workout made of repetitive exercises that strain some muscle groups and joints while neglecting others. We can easily overcome this by breaking up the day with micro-workouts or movement-snacks but we can also incorporate rich movement patterns into life through a little play and adventure. It might seem silly to be emptying the dishwasher while looking like I’m warming up for a Cossack dance - but this is exactly the kind of movement that keeps me in good mobility, flexibility, real world strength and is also a key contributor to all day energy and consistent mental clarity. When damaged, the process should take 9 to 12 months, depending on the goals and sport of the individual.   Although natural healing will occur, if you’re looking at returning to an active lifestyle or a return to sport it is crucial that you are guided through each step of the way and understand what you can or cannot tolerate at any given time. There are well researched guidelines and criteria that equate to whether or not you are fit to return, or whether you need to keep loading and getting stronger   All this week we are given you access to how we manage our ACL injuries and successfully guide our patients back to full health   Introducing new exercises can be daunting for physios and the patient, understanding what stresses are placed through the knee is so important.   The research surrounding ACLs provides us with substantial evidence to create and support goals and testing throughout each stage of the recovery. Most noticeably supporting big decisions such as:-   ‘’When can I return to running’ ‘’How do I know if it is safe to introduce a new movement’’ ‘’When can I start to load up my current rehab with weights’’   The take home message from this weeks content should be that time is only one small factor in your ACL recover!   Just because 12 months has passed doesn’t mean you are ready to return. If you haven’t received any objective measures, specific yes/no, pass/fail criteria throughout each stage of your rehab, you are increasing the risk of a secondary injury on returning to an active or sporting life. #acl #anteriorcruciateligament #knee #injured #injury #jointpain #leg #legday #legs #strengthday #strengthtraining #physio #pt #online #physiotherapy #physiotherapist #physicaltherapist #therapist #therapy #therapies #physiotherapie #fyp @Alex Chester

Lunges 🦵 Lunges are an exercise which be can great to work on strengthening the glutes, quads and calves. However far too often I see patients struggling to tolerate the load it’s placing on their knee and thus compensating movements occur which are exacerbating their pain.  Most common compensations I come across; 1. Knee Valgus- swinging of the knee inwards as you step into the lunge  2. Excessive pelvic drop of the opposite hip to side you are lunging on 3. Heel elevation of the lunging leg as you step into the lunge. 4. Knee hyperextension of the lunging leg in the final stage of the lunge where you are coming back upright  A Single Leg Press is a nice way to work on gradually building up the load tolerance of the knee in a more supportive environment. This support will allow you slow the movement down and focus on control whilst building up resistance in your own time. The video shows an incline leg press but due to its incline posture, it starts on about 20kg resistance which may be too much for some people . As an alternative, you can do a horizontal leg press which will be a significantly lower starting resistance. I personally love using the leg press, it’s a staple of my weekly leg workouts. #knees #lunges #physiotherapist #physiotherapy #rehabilitation #exercise #rehab #rehabilitation #exercisetherapy #healtheducation  #chronicpain #selfconfidence #conditioning #gym #walking #running #runners #strengthforrunners #marathon #parkrun #meniscus #acl #aclrehab #sport #lifestyle #strengthttraining#osteoarthritis #jointpain #tendon #foryou #foryoupage #nopain

When damaged, the process should take 9 to 12 months, depending on the goals and sport of the individual.   Although natural healing will occur, if you’re looking at returning to an active lifestyle or a return to sport it is crucial that you are guided through each step of the way and understand what you can or cannot tolerate at any given time. There are well researched guidelines and criteria that equate to whether or not you are fit to return, or whether you need to keep loading and getting stronger   All this week we are given you access to how we manage our ACL injuries and successfully guide our patients back to full health   Introducing new exercises can be daunting for physios and the patient, understanding what stresses are placed through the knee is so important.   The research surrounding ACLs provides us with substantial evidence to create and support goals and testing throughout each stage of the recovery. Most noticeably supporting big decisions such as:-   ‘’When can I return to running’ ‘’How do I know if it is safe to introduce a new movement’’ ‘’When can I start to load up my current rehab with weights’’   The take home message from this weeks content should be that time is only one small factor in your ACL recover!   Just because 12 months has passed doesn’t mean you are ready to return. If you haven’t received any objective measures, specific yes/no, pass/fail criteria throughout each stage of your rehab, you are increasing the risk of a secondary injury on returning to an active or sporting life. #acl #anteriorcruciateligament #knee #injured #injury #jointpain #leg #legday #legs #strengthday #strengthtraining #physio #pt #online #physiotherapy #physiotherapist #physicaltherapist #therapist #therapy #therapies #physiotherapie #fyp @Alex Chester

🧘🏽 Does Posture Matter? 🤷🏽‍♂️ Not as much as you'd think! We have been told that there are 'bad' postures - but what does that actually mean?  ‼️ Sitting slumped isn’t bad - Unless we sit slumped agressively fast and cause tissue damage. It takes a long long time of sitting in one position to feel pain because holding a position, unless very extreme, cannot rip or tear soft tissue. 💫 It actually seems that being too still for too long is the issue and not the position.  Find comfortable positions, find a comfortable chair - but keep moving! Lacking internal rotation in the shoulder, try this stretch!  This stretch is known as the couch stretch and is very good at opening up the internal rotation of the shoulder as it pins down the scapula so it can’t move by laying on it and stretching the posterior capsule of the shoulder, including the Teres Minor and infraspinatus muscles of the rotator cuff (Laudner et al., 2008).  This is important in overhead or throwing athletes, such as baseball players, swimmers, tennis and volley ball players to name a few. This can lead to impingement of the shoulder due to excessive repetitive movements, which can lead to what’s called internal impingement, which has been linked to a deficit in internal rotation of the shoulder (Burkhart et al., 2003). This can also be linked to weakness and instability around the shoulder and can be caused by or lead to rotator cuff pathologies as it is the tendons of the rotator cuff that are being impinged.  It is therefore important to keep the shoulder capsule stable and loose at the same time to help prevent injuries and this ‘Sleeper Stretch’ is a great tool to add to your toolbox or help prevent shoulder injuries. *Disclaimer - this is for educational purposes only and shouldn’t be done by anyone with long standing shoulder issues, acute shoulder issues or anyone who has a history of shoulder dislocation* #shoulder #shoulders #shoulderpain #shoulderpainrelief #shoulderstretch #jointpain #jointhealth #rotatorcuff #shoulderprehab #swimmer #throwing #injury #sportsinjuriesexpert #sportsinjuryrehab #rehab #rehabscience #rehabilitation #sports #sportstherapy #sportstherapist #prehab #prehabilitation #shoulderstability #shoulderstretch

Calf stretching is a crucial component of injury prevention for individuals aged 40 and above. As we age, muscle flexibility tends to decrease, making calf muscles more susceptible to strain and injury. A regular stretching routine can mitigate this risk. Simple exercises like the classic calf stretch, where you lean against a wall with one foot back, can help maintain calf muscle elasticity. These stretches increase blood flow, reduce muscle tightness, and improve range of motion. This is How the Knee Looks While Moving #anatomy The knee is a complex joint that plays a crucial role in our ability to move, walk, run, and perform various activities. Understanding its anatomy is essential for maintaining its health and preventing injuries. Here's an overview of the key components of the knee joint: 1. Bones: The knee joint is primarily composed of three bones: the femur (thighbone), the tibia (shinbone), and the patella (kneecap). These bones come together to form the knee joint. 2. Articular Cartilage: The ends of the femur, tibia, and the undersurface of the patella are covered with articular cartilage, a smooth, slippery tissue that allows the bones to glide smoothly against each other during movement. 3. Meniscus: Two wedge-shaped pieces of cartilage, known as menisci, act as cushions and shock absorbers within the knee joint. They help distribute weight evenly and stabilize the joint. 4. Ligaments: Several ligaments provide stability to the knee joint. The major ones include the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL), posterior cruciate ligament (PCL), medial collateral ligament (MCL), and lateral collateral ligament (LCL). 5. Patellar Tendon: This strong tendon connects the patella to the tibia and allows the knee to straighten. 6. Quadriceps Tendon: Located above the patella, this tendon connects the quadriceps muscle to the patella, allowing it to function effectively. 7. Bursae: Small, fluid-filled sacs called bursae reduce friction within the knee joint. They are located around the knee and provide lubrication. 8. Synovial Membrane: The inner lining of the joint capsule, called the synovial membrane, produces synovial fluid, which lubricates the joint and nourishes the articular cartilage. 9. Joint Capsule: The joint capsule is a fibrous structure that surrounds the knee joint, providing stability and protection. 10. Muscles: Various muscles, including the quadriceps, hamstrings, and calf muscles, play a critical role in moving and stabilizing the knee joint. Understanding the anatomy of the knee is essential for healthcare professionals, athletes, and anyone interested in maintaining knee health. Super excited that I’m currently training to become the first male menopause doula with The Menopause School - the menopause is an evolutionary trait found in humans and a few long lived whales. This evolutionary adaptation should be a gift to us, but our modern lives are not set up to facilitate the genetic expression and best outputs that our bodies and minds should be experiencing. This gets seriously compounded during peri-menopause and menopause… and even throughout specific parts of the menstrual cycle.  I’ve had a number of menstruating clients who have experienced a revolution in the negative symptoms they had come to associate with their period and also a number of peri and post-menopausal women find freedom from what they had believed was a new norm of poor sleep, aches and pains, brain fog, energy dips, mood fluctuations and weight gain.  I know many have had terrible experiences in this realm and I’m really not equipped to speak to this in any truly relational way and do not wish to diminish these experiences in any way, and, indeed, want to add to the conversation; offering that we don’t have to settle for what has become normal but perhaps isn’t natural.  If you’re experiencing negative symptoms or phenomenons that accompany your period or your experience of perimenopause, menopause or post-menopause - reach out! Do you suffer from back pain such as 85 % of people?  When my friend Becks @thehousebuild told me she was in pain with her sacroiliac joint pain, and that few of you asked me to design workouts for back problems, it became my mission to make a serie of videos to help you to understand the problem and how to treat it!  I came to Pilates 27 years ago because of back pain so this is indeed my area of expertise!  I am making OCTOBER my backcare month!  The sacroiliac joint is located in the pelvis, connecting the sacrum and ilium bones. Facts about sacroiliac joint pain include: 	1.	Location: The sacroiliac joint is at the base of the spine, connecting the sacrum (triangular bone at the bottom of the spine) and the ilium (part of the pelvis). 	2.	Function: It plays a crucial role in transferring forces between the upper body and legs, providing stability during activities like walking and standing. 	3.	Pain Symptoms: Sacroiliac joint pain is often felt as low back pain, buttock pain, or pain radiating down the leg. It can be mistaken for other spinal conditions. 	4.	Causes: Causes of sacroiliac joint pain include inflammation, injury, pregnancy-related changes, arthritis, or degenerative conditions. 	5.	Diagnosis: Diagnosing sacroiliac joint pain can be challenging as its symptoms overlap with other conditions.  	6.	Treatment: Exercise programs that strengthen the core and improve joint stability such as Pilates are recommended. Are you ready? Do your joints let you know when damp rainy weather is coming without you needing to see the forecast?  According to a study done by Harvard Medical School’s Professor Robert Jamison, 67.9% of people surveyed felt the same. He concluded that the increased pain may be due to a change in barometric pressure (atmospheric pressure), which normally pushes against the body from the outside. When the weather worsens, the barometric pressure falls, causing tissues in the body to expand and push on the nerve endings that signal pain. The good news is that Myofascial Release treatment can help to reduce the restrictions around your joints, giving more space for expansion without pushing on the nerve endings. 𝐆𝐲𝐦 𝐄𝐪𝐮𝐢𝐩𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐀𝐧𝐝 𝐇𝐨𝐰 𝐓𝐨 𝐔𝐬𝐞 𝐈𝐭: 𝐇𝐢𝐩 𝐓𝐡𝐫𝐮𝐬𝐭 𝐌𝐚𝐜𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐞  Today I’m gonna show you how to use the hip thrusts machine 😄 Now a lot of people thing this machine is just for women, but that really isn’t the case ❌ The glutes are part of the posterior chain which is the ground of muscles that run up the back of the body, if one part of that chain is weak then it will affect how your body mechanics function 🤯 So if you want to get stronger then you need to do direct glute work ✅ Here is the set up: - Sit on the bench making sure your lower body does not come off the pad. - Plant your feet shoulder width apart on the platform in a position you know when you are performing the exercise, heels won’t rise and your will contract more glute than hamstring. - Set up the belt were your hips hinge and tighten it so there’s no slack when unracking. - Begin by thrusting up and pushing the pins away, hands are now away and lower yourself into the movement. - Press through the platform with your feet and thrust towards the ceiling. - When finished stay in the high position, grab the pins and rerack the weight and unclip the belt. 𝐌𝐲𝐭𝐡 𝐁𝐮𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐫 𝐑𝐞𝐛𝐨𝐨𝐭: ‘𝐅𝐚𝐭 𝐈𝐬 𝐁𝐚𝐝’ 👀 Over the years I have seen plenty of macronutrients come under attack, especially fat ❌ But being a macronutrient… you NEED IT!!! We need fat because it is a secondary source of energy, protects our internal organs and it regulates hormone levels 🤯 So fat itself isn’t bad, it’s the sources in which you get it from ✅ If you get the majority of your fats from cakes, crisps, chocolate, fast food, vegetable oils..otherwise known as saturated fats and trans fats, these fats are not good for you 🙅🏼‍♂️ But if you are get your fat from nut/seeds, oils (olive, almond), avocados, fatty fish, these have unsaturated fats which are good for you 😊 Some saturated fats like the ones you get from red meat aren’t the worst and some nuts such as Brazil nuts if you eat more than four can actually be toxic 😅 The devil really is in the dose, but we want more unsaturated than saturated fats 🫒🥑 So swapping out vegetable for olives oil, adding avocado dishes into your weekly diet, and less fast food and snacks for fatty fish and lower calorie snacks would be beneficial 🙌🏼 If you want help with your diet and weight loss then click the link in my bio to book a call or DM me the word ‘READY’ for a free consultation 🚀 #strengthcoach #pt #musclebuilding  #strengthtraining #sportperformance  #weightloss #fitness #health #mobility #transformation #jointpain #kneepain  #backpain #shoulderpain #hippain #elbowpain  #mindset #healthylifestyle #motivation #selfimprovement #fitfam #irishfitfam #ukfitfam #gymbeginners #beginnerlifters #lightweight #lifting #club24fitnesslisburn

Asking the Right Questions Before Supplying Aspirin: What Your Doctor or Pharmacist Needs to Know  As a experienced pharmacist, it's imperative to conduct a thorough patient assessment before supplying aspirin, a widely used analgesic and anti-inflammatory medication.  Key questions address potential allergies, existing medical conditions like stomach ulcers or bleeding disorders, and concurrent medication use, crucial for preventing adverse reactions.  Inquiring about alcohol consumption is vital due to the increased risk of gastrointestinal bleeding when aspirin is combined with alcohol.  These questions are essential for ensuring patient safety, optimizing therapeutic outcomes, and adhering to best practices in pharmaceutical care. When it gets chillier and the nights draw in, remember to look after your joints. The cold and damp can really hike up the chances of aches and pains in your joints.  The reason behind this? It's often put down to the barometric pressure dropping. This leads to your body's tissues puffing up, causing a fair bit of joint pain, especially if you've got arthritis. Here are 4 tips to weather-proof your joints this winter: • Stay warm - do this by wearing several layers. You can also apply heat pads to hot water bottles to help relax your muscles • Stay hydrated. Central heating is drying so ensure you drink lots of water to keep your joints lubricated. • Loosen stiff joints by moving around. Exercise is great, and will warm you up, but if you can't exercise then simple activities like getting up and walking around in the tv ad breaks will still be useful. • For chronic pain, Myofascial Release can help by gently warming the trigger areas and releasing restrictions. The lady in the video if you don't already know is an eyelash technician, I shouldn't have to tell you that all day every day she's in the chin to chest position (Kyphotic) which can cause all sorts of issues.   ➡️One of the main health issues associated with being in a kyphotic position, such as slouching or hunching forward, all day for work is the increased risk of developing musculoskeletal disorders. ➡️Maintaining an unnatural curvature in the spine puts excessive strain on the neck, upper back, and shoulder muscles, leading to chronic pain and discomfort. This prolonged poor posture can cause structural imbalances in the spine and misalignment of the vertebrae, potentially resulting in conditions like kyphosis or herniated discs. ➡️Additionally, sitting with a rounded back can compress vital organs and reduce lung capacity, leading to shallow breathing patterns and decreased oxygen intake. Over time, this may result in respiratory problems and reduced cardiovascular health. ➡️The lack of support for the spinal column due to poor posture also increases stress on the intervertebral discs, increasing the risk of disc degeneration and potential nerve impingement. Therefore, it is crucial for individuals in professional settings to be aware of their posture throughout the day and take necessary steps to improve ergonomics to alleviate these health risks. Some poteial ailments may include, ➡️Neck and upper thoracic pain. ➡️Stiffness, ➡️Cervicogenic headaches and Migranes, ➡️TMJ/Temporomandibular joint dysfunction, ➡️Thoracic outlet syndrome, ➡️Neuralgia, ➡️Numbness and tingling down the arms/hands. ➡️Symptoms of carpal tunnel. ➡️Loss of power and mobility to upper peripherals/arms. ➡️Joint dysfunction, ➡️Inflammation, that deep bruised feeling, often on the upper traps/shoulders. ➡️Lower back pain, ➡️Sciatic symptoms. Wow 2023 what a year!  Jan / Feb opticians spotted Grade 3/4 Papilledema - the swelling around my optic discs was so severe my vision was failing.  An emergency hospital admission followed and a diagnosis of Idiopathic Intercranial Hypertension was made and at the same time an MRI identified herniated discs in my neck and spinal cord compression (all contributing to my dizziness, pain, fatigue etc) The next 6/7 months were a real struggle to get medication levels right, deal with after effects of how ill I’d been, waiting for my vision to return (thankfully it has), getting to understand my condition, my medication, the side effects, my limitations. The biggest challenge though, was getting my confidence back!  I am not the person I was before diagnosis. But I have now been able to meet myself where I am at instead of trying to be who I was. The Joint Pain Programme at Nuffield Health @nhcottingley was a huge support, it helped me to get out of the house, to get active, to accept my limits, to work with them and start to progress beyond them!  I have been able to embrace my love of exercise again - no I can’t squat double body weight, I can’t swim a mile in one session, I have to have full rest days sometimes two or three rest days in a row BUT THAT IS OK!  Now the programme has come to an end, I am back to my normal working hours so the new challenge begins - managing my new “daily normal”  Too often this has been where I fall down, so with inspiration and support from Dad my new daily mantra is Am I MAD? (my dads initials)  Instagram / Twitter / Threads / TikTok are packed full of useful information about health, exercise, what to do, what not to do - but there is just TOO MUCH information!  It’s overwhelming! (Especially for neurospicy me!) So I have gone ok let’s keep it simple!  So every day, I will be checking - Am I MAD?  Am I Moving?  Am I (holding myself) Accountable? Am I Documenting Daily?  Nothing else, no other goals - just to move and write down what I am doing! (Using my @justworkwithjay  Lifestyle Planner 😉) Then we build from there!  #health #neurospicy #adhd #iih #jointpain #movemore #inspiredbydad #amimad

Here's a basic recipe for pork leg jelly: ( you could also use turkey leg instead.. adjusting accordingly) **Ingredients:** - 2 pork trotters or pork leg segments - 1 onion, chopped - 2 carrots, chopped - 3-4 cloves of garlic, minced - Fresh herbs like thyme or bay leaves - Salt and pepper to taste - Water **Instructions:** 1. **Prepare the Pork:**    - Clean and rinse the pork trotters thoroughly. 2. **Boil the Pork:**    - Place the pork trotters in a large pot, cover with water, and bring to a boil.    - Once boiling, discard the water and rinse the trotters to remove impurities. 3. **Simmer with Vegetables:**    - Place the cleaned trotters back into the pot.    - Add chopped onion, carrots, minced garlic, and your choice of herbs.    - Season with salt and pepper. 4. **Simmer Until Tender:**    - Fill the pot with enough water to cover the trotters and vegetables.    - Simmer on low heat for 2-3 hours or until the pork is tender and the collagen has broken down. 5. **Strain and Set:**    - Once cooked, strain the liquid to separate the jelly from the solids.    - Allow the liquid to cool and refrigerate until it solidifies into a jelly-like consistency. 6. **Serve:**    - Slice the chilled jelly and serve it on its own or with condiments like mustard or vinegar. Remember to customize the recipe according to your preferences, and enjoy your homemade pork leg jelly! Pork leg jelly, also known as pork hock jelly or pork trotter jelly, is a dish made by simmering pork leg or trotters until the collagen-rich connective tissues break down, resulting in a gelatinous texture. It's often flavored with herbs, spices, and sometimes vinegar. The collagen released during cooking gives the dish a thick, jellied consistency when cooled. It's popular in various cuisines and is believed by some to have health benefits for joints and skin due to the collagen content. Pork leg jelly, being rich in collagen obtained from simmered connective tissues, may offer several potential benefits: 1. **Joint Health:** Collagen is a key component of joints, and consuming it may support joint health and reduce joint pain. 2. **Skin Health:** Collagen is known for promoting skin elasticity and hydration, potentially benefiting skin health. 3. **Bone Health:** The dish often includes bones, providing minerals like calcium and phosphorus, which are crucial for bone strength. 4. **Digestive Health:** The gelatin in the jelly may support digestive health by promoting a healthy gut lining. 5. **Nutrient Absorption:** The slow cooking process may extract nutrients from bones and connective tissues, making them more bioavailable. While these potential benefits exist, individual responses vary. Your health doesn't solely depend on anyone! It has always been in your hands.  I view accumulating symptoms as "messages" your body is telling you subtly, something needs to be looked at.  Rather than constantly suppress them with pills I may have been dealt a shitty hand from the get go  That doesn’t mean I wallow in self pity  My changes didn't come from pills They came from being a fierce advocate for my OWN health It was only then, that things started to make sense Understanding pain is key here,  🗣️Pain is a protective mechanism, an alarm system. 🗣️Pain is a brain output, not a tissue input. 🗣️Pain involves various brain areas, not just a specific 'pain region.' 🗣️As pain persists the nervous  system gets better at producing it  🗣️Tissue damage doesn't always equal pain. 🗣️Hurt doesn't necessarily mean harm. (Ever hit your funny bome)  🗣️Pain shouldn't guide all your decisions 🗣️Pain is influenced by attitudes, beliefs, and environment. Our Thoughts impact our pain perception 🗣️Stress and sleep significantly affect pain 🗣️The brain is changeable; even after years of pain Even if we have been in pain for years, we can always find ways to create new pathways in the brain which can improve our perception of pain. 🦿For someone with “Osteoarthritis” This is some of my warm up to most sessions especially before running or a leg session.  The reason I have put #osteoarthritis in inverted commas is because I didn’t accept the diagnosis! and if I did I probably wouldn’t of ever ran or competed in anything ever again. Doctors said it will only degenerate and get worse over time leading to a hip replacement before I was 35…well I’m 34 now and it’s feeling better every month.  The problem is the mainstream idea that the damage on the bone is irreversible and degenerative. It’s not!! There are so many new studies that point to inactivity and “rest” accelerating the issue! It’s usually the case that the thing that you avoid is often the cure.  I have made stretching and strengthening all around the hip from the lower back to the feet a priority to get back my functionality and mobility couple this with @truelightsuk therapy to improve healing I have gone from complete inactivity and pain everyday to a mild pain (that is getting less each month ) after a long run or heavy leg day but I expect this to be gone in another 6 months. I’m not gonna lie it took me the best part of 2 years to get to this point so if your looking for a short cut to recover your joint pain then your not gonna get there and if someone tells you otherwise it’s a lie.  There are ways of finding temporary relief like with acupuncture or massage or from a chiropractor but while these may allow some short term relief if you don’t then reset and build the muscles up around the joint then you will be back to square one in no time. You literally have to start from the ground up that means start at your feet and work your way up to your neck. Treat your body like you are relearning how to move becuase essentially the pains we have are usually a muscle weakness and not joint related. The joint gets damaged later on but again can be rectified if persistent action is taken. A before and after of a treatment performed today on our patient Gemma. We love to see the before and after from a mobility perspective, however our biggest goal is to reduce pain. So, let's talk about how our therapies can help bring down the intensity of pain. When it comes to spinal manipulation, massage, and acupuncture – these practices have been found to downregulate pain signals in our bodies. You see, the nervous system plays a significant role in transmitting pain messages to our brains. By engaging in spinal manipulation or  adjustments, pressure on the nerves surrounding the spine is reduced, promoting better nerve function and decreasing pain response. Massages, on the other hand, relieve tension and muscle tightness that can contribute to discomfort. They stimulate blood flow and release endorphins – those natural feel-good chemicals – which in turn help alleviate pain sensation. And then there's acupuncture, where thin needles are inserted into specific points along energy pathways known as meridians. This stimulates the release of various neurotransmitters and hormones that dampen pain signals and enhance overall well-being. Here are some of the potential consequences: 1. Osteoporosis: Estrogen plays a critical role in maintaining bone density. Chronic estrogen deficiency can lead to a significant decrease in bone density, increasing the risk of osteoporosis and fractures. 2. Cardiovascular Disease: Estrogen is believed to have a protective effect on the heart and blood vessels. Long-term deficiency may contribute to an increased risk of cardiovascular diseases, including heart attacks and strokes. 3. Urogenital Atrophy: Estrogen helps maintain the health of the vaginal and urinary tracts. Chronic deficiency can lead to vaginal dryness, atrophy, and an increased risk of urinary tract infections. 4. Skin Changes: Estrogen deficiency can result in thinner, less elastic skin, and an increase in wrinkles and skin dryness. 5. Sexual Dysfunction: Low estrogen levels can lead to decreased libido, painful intercourse due to vaginal dryness, and an overall decrease in sexual function. 6. Stomach pain, bloating, gas, constipation and dhiarrohea… When you’re dealing with these, you’re also dealing with a poor functioning immune system.  Obstacle #1- Knowing what to eat  If you’ve just started to make the connection between food and your symptoms, here’s where to start: . Try and eat mainly whole foods . Limit foods that come out of a box or bag  . Reduce histamine load through food  Testing for food sensitivities is helpful.  Obstacle #2- Figuring out what supplements are helpful  Supplements can be daunting, it can be hard knowing what to take, here’s where to start: . Magnesium (calm stress) . Vitamin c (immune system) . Zinc (gut/immune system) . Digestive enzymes (break down food) You can run a test to find out your unique deficiencies.  Obstacle #3- Finding the true root causes  You must address the ‘why’, which can be: . Too much Bacteria/yeast inside your gut . Parasites . Heavy metals (mercury/arsenic/lead) . Medication overuse  . Environmental toxicity (mold/chemicals) You can test for all of the above. Do you suffer often sufffer from the crippling hidden pains of IBS? Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a common disorder that affects the large intestine (colon). While the exact cause of IBS is unknown, it's believed to involve multiple factors including abnormal muscle contractions in the intestines, inflammation, and changes in gut microbiota. The signs and symptoms of IBS can vary widely among individuals, but some hidden signs or less obvious manifestations of IBS may include: Fatigue: Many individuals with IBS report feeling unusually tired, even after a full night's sleep. This fatigue can be related to disrupted sleep patterns due to gastrointestinal symptoms such as pain or diarrhea, or it may be a result of the body's response to chronic stress and discomfort associated with IBS. Joint and Muscle Pain: Some people with IBS may experience joint or muscle pain that seems unrelated to their digestive symptoms. The exact mechanisms behind this are not fully understood, but it may be related to inflammation or changes in immune function associated with IBS. Headaches: Chronic headaches or migraines are reported by some individuals with IBS. The connection between IBS and headaches is not entirely clear, but it's believed that disruptions in the gut-brain axis, as well as shared neurotransmitters and inflammatory mediators, may play a role. #IBS #IrritableBowelSyndrome #HiddenPains #DigestiveDisorder #ChronicFatigue #GutHealth #AbnormalMuscleContractions #Inflammation #MicrobiotaChanges #GastrointestinalSymptoms #PainManagement #IBSAwareness #FatigueFactors #SleepDisturbances #ChronicStress #JointPain #MusclePain #Discomfort #InvisibleIllness #MentalHealthImpact #IBSSupport #PainfulDays #WellnessJourney #IBSCommunity

As today 29th February is National Rare Disease day I thought I would publicly for the 1st time raise awareness of the autoimmune condition/disease I was finally diagnosed with last October after 4/5 long years of  being plagued with illness.... Behćets Disease /disorder/syndrome. Behcet's syndrome, is a rare disorder that causes blood vessel inflammation throughout your body. And not just large vessels, the large  right the ways through to smallest. the pain can be unbearable. I have never publicly discussed this disease due to the embarrassing symptoms listed causing immediate judgement. my symptoms of this can come and go. At the moment I am managing as my most recent flare is somewhat under control however, the drugs I have to take daily for this are highly toxic so I have to have my kidney and liver function monitored regularly and the side effects to the drugs can be not very nice at all. We shouldn't have to be worried or ashamed of our illnesses. It was a very long processed to get the diagnosis with this illness. it is said to have looked to have onset of this around 4 years ago/5. The symptoms can be mild and minor or severe they can change regularly masking itself almost as the symptom being an isolated illness alone when in actual fact its a symptomsof a flare. Around 4 in 5 adults (that’s a whopping 80 per cent) of adults experience low back pain at some point in their lifetimes.  It is the most common cause of job-related disability and a leading contributor to missed work days.  In a recent survey of thousands of people, more than a quarter of adults reported experiencing low back pain during the past 3 months. You are not alone, but of course the severity and duration of pain varies immensely.  Men and women are equally affected by low back pain, which can range in intensity from a dull, constant ache to a sudden, sharp sensation that leaves the person incapacitated.  Pain can begin abruptly as a result of an accident or by lifting something heavy, or it can develop over time due to age-related changes of the spine. Sedentary lifestyles can set the stage for low back pain, especially when a weekday routine of getting too little exercise is punctuated by strenuous weekend workout!  Most back pain is acute, or short term, and lasts a few days to a few weeks. It tends to resolve on its own with self-care and there is no residual loss of function. The majority of acute low back pain is mechanical in nature, meaning that there is a disruption in the way the components of the back (the spine, muscle, intervertebral discs, and nerves) fit together and move. Subacute low back pain is defined as pain that lasts between 4 and 12 weeks. Though there is a long list of other back and spine pain which may be chronic and last a much longer time. A hypermobile joint can bend beyond the typical range of movement. Many people are hypermobile (around 1 in 10) – and hypermobility is more common in women and children, and people of Afro-Caribbean and Asian descent. It is common in gymnasts, athletes, dancers and musicians. Many hypermobile people have no significant symptoms (‘asymptomatic hypermobility’). For a smaller number of people hypermobility is accompanied by symptoms (symptomatic hypermobility) Some conditions which often exist alongside hypermobility include: Autism, autonomic dysfunction, mast cell activation disorders, anxiety and depression and fibromyalgia. What is the best workout frequency for strength training? 1, 3, or 5 workouts a week? What’s the best? Exercise is really similar to medication.  If you have an appropriate dose, we need to determine the appropriate dose frequency. Exercise can do two things: make a positive change or interfere with the adoption process if the stimulus is brought back too early.    If the exercise is extremely intense, we have to reduce the frequency in order to not interfere with the adaptation process.  But if you don’t push yourself hard enough, you’ll be able to handle higher frequencies. But the goal of going to the gym is to push hard really.   According to the vast majority of studies, how often you work out makes very little or no difference in your progress.    If you truly push yourself, going once a week can be enough. If you’re just moving objects around aimlessly without progression, more work will be required.   But everyone’s tolerance for frequency and volume is different. Just because something works for a few people, it’s not guaranteed it’ll work for you. #strenghttraining #strengthandconditioning #workout #workoutroutine #frequency #volume #gym #gymmotivation #exercise #fatloss #weightloss #weightlossjourney #diet #dietplan #healtyfood #barbell #shoulderworkout #shoulderrehab #homeworkout #getstrong #gymforbeginners #startworkout #weightlifting #getstrong #hittraining #sport #kneepain #jointpain #rehabilitation

Genetic mutations affect collagen production or structure, weakening connective tissues.  The Beighton score helps diagnose it by assessing joint flexibility out of 9 points.  Management includes physical therapy and lifestyle adjustments. Why do my muscles hurt after exercise? If you try a new physical activity, or change your exercise routine, you may experience Delayed-Onset Muscle Soreness (DOMS). These muscle aches may come on 6 to 12 hours after a workout and can last from 48 hours and up to 5 days. The pain you experience with DOMS is caused by tiny, microscopic tears in your muscle fibres which your body responds to by increasing inflammation. Ehlers can be responsible for a wide range of symptoms from joint pain to gut disorders, easy bruising and lots lots more. Ehlers is something I've personally struggled with, I have it quite severely - my joints bend back around 45 degrees. I was fortunately diagnosed young and sent to ballet class to strengthen me up. If you live with inflammatory arthritis and stumble upon someone online claiming that one thing has cured or improved their arthritis, then run a mile because they're likely trying to sell you something or they're downplaying all the other things they've done in conjunction with that one thing to improve their symptoms. When it comes to recovering a better quality of life with arthritis, we want to take a multifaceted approach, looking at the whole person—mind, body, soul. That's why there's no one diet for arthritis, no one exercise for arthritis, and no one supplement for arthritis. It depends on the person, and most importantly, we also want to consider other small individual factors like their environment, age, and much more. So, it's always good to work with someone one-to-one or make sure that you get your sources from a variety of places and always start with first principal thinking to strategize for arthritis, rather than trying to go all in on one thing. #ankylosingspondylitis #rheumatoidarthritis #arthritis #jointpain #healthcoach

✨Pain-Free Feet, Ankles & Knees✨ Simple exercises for healthy feet, ankles and knees that can be done anywhere anytime. 1. Calf Raises on a step for a full range of motion, but if that’s too much substitute with floor calf raises. 2. Foot rolling on a tenis ball/small ball - relieves foot pain (plantar fasciitis), improves circulation and balance, improves foot mobility, prevents injuries, improves sleep. 3. Toe curls with a towel - doing toe curls builds up the flexor muscles of the toes and feet, improving overall strength. 4. Ankle Strength + Stretch with a band - Sit on the floor with your leg out straight. Place an exercise band around the ball of your foot, hold on to it with both hands, and push away creating resistance in the band. This exercise will help strengthen the calf muscle, and other muscles around the lower leg and ankle. For the ankle stretch pull the band towards you.  ✅Save / Share / Follow for more tips & exercises #plantarfasciitis #plantarfasciitisrelief #foothealth #barefooted #footpain #anklemobility #anklestability #anklerehab #footcare #footmobility #anklepain #kneestrengthening #kneehealth #physio #jointhealth #jointpain #mobility #runnerproblems #podiatry #strongfeet

Medical acupuncture or dry needling consists of the insertion of needles into the skin and the muscle. It has been shown to elicit various benefits, so let’s go through some: -	Pail relief: this is achieved through the stimulation of nociceptors and mechanoreceptors within the tissue which are responsible for detecting painful stimuli. -	Increased blood flow: the needles stimulate vasodilation (dilation of the blood vessels) leading to increased blood flow and oxygenation. -	Local twitch response: when the needle is pulsated (as shown in the video) this causes an involuntary spinal reflex /contraction which can alter the length and tension of muscle fibres -	Increase range of motion: this can occur as a subsequent effect of the increased blood flow and the twitch response. -	Neurophysiological effects: similar to the twitch response, the needle can cause homeostasis at the targeted site which leads to decrease central and peripheral sensitisation to pain. 1. Create a Calorie Deficit: To lose weight faster, you need to consume fewer calories than you burn. Calculate your daily calorie needs and create a calorie deficit by reducing your calorie intake or increasing your physical activity. 2. Eat a Balanced Diet: Focus on consuming nutrient-dense foods such as fruits, vegetables, lean proteins, whole grains, and healthy fats. Avoid processed foods, sugary drinks, and excessive amounts of added sugars and unhealthy fats. 3. Increase Protein Intake: Protein can help reduce appetite, boost metabolism, and preserve muscle mass. Include lean sources of protein like chicken, fish, tofu, beans, and Greek yogurt in your meals and snacks. 4. Stay Hydrated: Drinking plenty of water can help boost metabolism, reduce calorie intake, and promote overall health. Aim to drink at least 8 cups (64 ounces) of water per day. 5. Engage in Regular Physical Activity: Incorporate both cardiovascular exercises (such as brisk walking, jogging, or cycling) and strength training exercises (like weightlifting or bodyweight exercises) into your routine. This helps burn calories, build muscle, and increase metabolism. 6. Get Enough Sleep: Lack of sleep can disrupt hormone levels, increase appetite, and hinder weight loss efforts. Aim for 7-9 hours of quality sleep each night to support weight loss and overall well-being. Remember, losing weight in a healthy and sustainable way takes time and consistency. Aim for at least 30 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise, such as brisk walking, jogging, or cycling, most days of the week. 2. Practice relaxation techniques: Techniques like deep breathing, meditation, yoga, and progressive muscle relaxation can help activate the body’s relaxation response, reducing cortisol levels and promoting a sense of calm. 3. Prioritize quality sleep: Adequate sleep is crucial for cortisol regulation. Aim for 7-9 hours of uninterrupted sleep each night. Establish a bedtime routine, create a sleep-friendly environment, and limit screen time before bed to improve the quality of your sleep. 4. Manage stress effectively: Identify the stressors in your life and find healthy ways to manage them. This may include setting boundaries, practicing time management, seeking support from loved ones, or engaging in activities you enjoy. 5. Maintain a balanced diet: Eat a well-balanced diet that includes plenty of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, and healthy fats. Avoid excessive caffeine and refined sugars, as they can contribute to cortisol spikes. When you have PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome), it is generally recommended to limit or avoid certain fruits that are high in sugar or have a high glycemic index. These fruits can cause a rapid increase in blood sugar levels and may worsen insulin resistance, which is common in PCOS. Here are some fruits that you may want to limit or avoid: 1. Bananas: Although bananas are a good source of nutrients, they are also high in sugar and carbohydrates. It’s best to consume them in moderation. 2. Grapes: Grapes are another fruit that is high in sugar. They also have a high glycemic index, which means they can cause a spike in blood sugar levels. 3. Mangoes: Mangoes are delicious, but they are also high in sugar. It’s recommended to consume them in moderation or opt for lower-sugar fruits instead. 4. Pineapple: Pineapple is a tropical fruit that contains a significant amount of sugar. Limit your intake or choose other fruits with lower sugar content. 5. Watermelon: Watermelon is refreshing, but it is also high in sugar and has a high glycemic index. Sure! Here are some strategies to optimize cortisol levels and manage stress: 1. Exercise regularly: Engaging in physical activity can help reduce cortisol levels and improve your mood. Aim for at least 30 minutes of moderate-intensity exercise, such as brisk walking, jogging, or cycling, most days of the week. 2. Practice relaxation techniques: Techniques like deep breathing, meditation, yoga, and progressive muscle relaxation can help activate the body’s relaxation response, reducing cortisol levels and promoting a sense of calm. 3. Prioritize quality sleep: Adequate sleep is crucial for cortisol regulation. Aim for 7-9 hours of uninterrupted sleep each night. Establish a bedtime routine, create a sleep-friendly environment, and limit screen time before bed to improve the quality of your sleep. 4. Manage stress effectively: Identify the stressors in your life and find healthy ways to manage them. This may include setting boundaries, practicing time management, seeking support from loved ones, or engaging in activities you enjoy. 5. Maintain a balanced diet: Eat a well-balanced diet that includes plenty of fruits, vegetables, whole grains, lean proteins, and healthy fats. Avoid excessive caffeine and refined sugars, as they can contribute to cortisol spikes. Today is the 4th July my reverse Independence Day, as today is my #strokeversary  It’s been 13 years since that holiday with my friends, where I was just having fun until suddenly.. I wasn’t. I’ve posted this picture many times and yes this is me physically having a stroke.  Spanish doctors said it was alcohol poisoning, I carried on my holiday for 3 days! When I got home I was hospitalised immediately. I was diagnosed with an #ischemicstroke they ran more tests and found over 9 #tia, some more tests later and finally conclusive diagnosis of #antiphospholipidantibodysyndrome #sneddonsyndrome version.  This diagnosis changed my life forever, the issues this condition has caused, the secondary conditions I have due to this, the side effects the medicines, the list is endless and every year that passes new diagnosis, new issues, new symptoms. It’s exhaustive.  I have been exceptionally lucky that I have an amazing husband and majority of my family have been there throughout to care for me, help and guide me; but also I have exceptional medical care from the 5 hospitals that help treat me with 9 different APS and related conditions specialist doctors. I had to fight for this but once I got it, I know I’m being looked after properly.  I’ve fought so hard through all of this hell and continue to fight everyday for the life I have managed to achieve. To onlookers I probably look as though my life never moved on, I was never able to have a life like my peers. Here are some of her most frequently asked questions about sports massage! 💆🏼 - Does Sports Massage have to hurt?  No! Sports massage is intended to be a deep and thorough treatment working to reduce knots and tension, which can be quite sore. However, if you have a slightly lower pain tolerance or a really tricky spot just let Katie know and she will tailor the treatment to you.  💆🏼 - I don’t play any sport, do I still qualify for Sports Massage?  Absolutely, regardless of how activity levels, anyone can and should come for a sports massage. There’s always somewhere to work on! 💆🏼- How long should I book in for? That all depends on what you’d like to have done. If you’d like some neck and shoulder relief or one specific area then 30 minutes is plenty. However, if you’d like to include your mid to lower back or include 2-3 areas, 60 minutes would be much more beneficial.  💆🏼- I suffer from headaches and the GP has said my muscles are tense, can you help? Yes! Massage is great for relieving all of the muscles in your neck / shoulders, reducing headaches and helping patients to come off of painkillers prescribed by the GP. 💆🏼- I don’t have an injury, but have recently started running 2-3 times a week. Would I benefit from some regular treatment and how often? Maintenance massages are a really great way to keep everything ticking over nicely and prevent future injuries. Maintenance massages should be booked between 6 and 8 weeks and could be 30 or 60 minutes. When you have PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome), it is generally recommended to limit or avoid certain fruits that are high in sugar or have a high glycemic index. These fruits can cause a rapid increase in blood sugar levels and may worsen insulin resistance, which is common in PCOS. Here are some fruits that you may want to limit or avoid: 1. Bananas: Although bananas are a good source of nutrients, they are also high in sugar and carbohydrates. It’s best to consume them in moderation. 2. Grapes: Grapes are another fruit that is high in sugar. They also have a high glycemic index, which means they can cause a spike in blood sugar levels. 3. Mangoes: Mangoes are delicious, but they are also high in sugar. It’s recommended to consume them in moderation or opt for lower-sugar fruits instead. 4. Pineapple: Pineapple is a tropical fruit that contains a significant amount of sugar. Limit your intake or choose other fruits with lower sugar content. 5. Watermelon: Watermelon is refreshing, but it is also high in sugar and has a high glycemic index. Moderation is key when consuming watermelon. “🚫 Fruits to Avoid with PCOS 🍌🍇🥭🍍🍉 When dealing with PCOS, it’s important to watch your fruit choices! Limit or skip these high-sugar fruits to keep your blood sugar in check and manage insulin resistance. During perimenopause, which typically occurs from the late 30s to mid-40s, a woman's bone health deteriorates at its fastest rate in her entire life. This rapid decline is due to the presence of oestrogen receptors in our bones, and as oestrogen levels decrease during menopause, bone density is significantly affected. Consequently, joint pain becomes very common during this period. Oestrogen acts as an anti-inflammatory hormone. As its levels drop, inflammation increases, leading to joint pain among other symptoms. 🧡Strategies to Alleviate Joint Pain - 1. Consume a Nutrient Dense Diet (preferably from real food, not supplements): - Calcium: Essential for bone health. - Magnesium: Helps maintain bone density. - Vitamin D: Aids in calcium absorption. - Protein: Supports overall bone structure. 2. Include Resistance Training in Your Exercise Routine: - Helps strengthen bones and joints. 3. Avoid restricting food groups, as they can negatively impact bone health. 🧀Foods High in Calcium: - Yoghurt - Poppy seeds - Beans and lentils - Cheese - Whey protein - Spinach - Fortified foods like cereal - Dairy products - Tofu - Edamame 🍌Foods High in Magnesium: - Spinach - Avocado - Chia seeds - Flaxseed - Nuts - Bananas - Dark chocolate - Oats - Fatty fish - Beans  🐠Foods High in Vitamin D: - Fatty fish (such as salmon, mackerel, and tuna) - Cod liver oil - Fortified dairy products (milk, yogurt) - Fortified plant-based milks (soy, almond, oat milk) - Fortified orange juice - Egg yolks - Cheese - Beef liver - Mushrooms exposed to sunlight 🍗Foods High in Protein: - Chicken - Lean beef - Whey protein - Beans and tofu - Fish - Pumpkin seeds - Eggs - Cottage cheese - Greek yogurt - Milk Your future health is shaped by the actions you take now. 10 Menopause weight loss thoughts whilst drinking my Tuesday cuppa… Average weight gain for perimenopausal women per year is 1.5kg, accumulating to 10 kg on reaching menopause.   So… 1️⃣ The real reason you’re gaining weight is down to body composition changing and losing muscle mass from 35+ not menopause or HRT. 2️⃣ However perimenopause symptoms such as sleep disturbance aid the desire to eat more and make poorer food choices. 3️⃣ Menopause is puberty in reverse, you wouldn’t tell a teenage girl to fast, do keto or restrict calories.  Menopause needs to be fuelled not starved. 4️⃣ The quality of food is 100% related to perimenopause symptoms and fat loss. 5️⃣ Protein is the nutrition secret to successful hormone function, improved symptoms and fat loss. 6️⃣ Resistance training is the exercise secret to maintaining body weight, muscle mass and strength in menopause. 7️⃣ The skills required for fat loss are different for maintaining weight long term. 8️⃣ A calorie does NOT equal a calorie in perimenopause. 9️⃣ Free yourself from the scales and use photos/measurements to track fat loss. 🔟 Shifting your mindset from a short term weight loss goal to a long term health goal will give you a clearer vision of who you want to be and how you can get there. Arthritis is a common condition that causes pain and inflammation in the joints. Here are five key signs of arthritis: 1. **Joint Pain**:    - Persistent or recurring pain in one or more joints, which may be worse after activity or at the end of the day. 2. **Joint Stiffness**:    - Stiffness in the joints, especially in the morning or after periods of inactivity. This stiffness can last for an hour or more. 3. **Swelling**:    - Swelling around the affected joints, often accompanied by warmth and redness. 4. **Reduced Range of Motion**:    - Difficulty moving the joints freely, leading to a decreased range of motion. This can make daily activities more challenging. 5. **Joint Deformity**:    - In advanced stages of arthritis, joints may become deformed or misaligned due to the ongoing damage. If you or someone you know is experiencing these signs, it's important to consult a healthcare professional for an accurate diagnosis and appropriate treatment.#arthritis #jointpain #stiff #swelling #motion #deformity #fyp #foryou #viral #body

Sent from my iPhone Radiofrequency (RF) therapy is a minimally invasive treatment option that uses radiofrequency energy to target nerves and tissues to provide relief from chronic pain and muscle discomfort. This treatment is typically used for conditions such as chronic pain, muscle spasms, arthritis, and nerve pain. Here is how RF therapy works for pain and muscle relief: 1. **Application**: A specialized RF machine is used to deliver controlled radiofrequency energy through a needle-like probe to the targeted area of pain or muscle tightness. 2. **Heat Generation**: The radiofrequency energy generates heat, which helps to disrupt the nerve signals responsible for transmitting pain sensations or relax tight muscles. 3. **Nerve Ablation**: In some cases, RF therapy can be used for nerve ablation, where the targeted nerves are heated to interrupt their ability to transmit pain signals effectively. This procedure can provide longer-lasting pain relief. 4. **Muscle Relaxation**: The heat generated by RF therapy can also help relax tight muscles by increasing blood flow, reducing inflammation, and promoting tissue healing. 5. **Pain Relief**: By disrupting pain signals or relaxing tight muscles, RF therapy can help reduce pain, improve range of motion, and enhance overall function in the targeted area. #radiofrequency #therapy #jointpain

When you have PCOS (Polycystic Ovary Syndrome), it is generally recommended to limit or avoid certain fruits that are high in sugar or have a high glycemic index. These fruits can cause a rapid increase in blood sugar levels and may worsen insulin resistance, which is common in PCOS. Here are some fruits that you may want to limit or avoid: 1. Bananas: Although bananas are a good source of nutrients, they are also high in sugar and carbohydrates. It’s best to consume them in moderation. 2. Grapes: Grapes are another fruit that is high in sugar. They also have a high glycemic index, which means they can cause a spike in blood sugar levels. 3. Mangoes: Mangoes are delicious, but they are also high in sugar. It’s recommended to consume them in moderation or opt for lower-sugar fruits instead. 4. Pineapple: Pineapple is a tropical fruit that contains a significant amount of sugar. Limit your intake or choose other fruits with lower sugar content. 5. Watermelon: Watermelon is refreshing, but it is also high in sugar and has a high glycemic index. Myofascial release. Many people have not heard of this technique or know what it is - so here is some more information!  Myofascial release using spiky massage balls is a self-care technique that involves using massage balls (the same technique can be carried out using a tennis ball or other small hard ball) to apply gentle pressure to the fascia (the connective tissue that surrounds and supports muscles). The goal of myofascial release is to release tension in the fascia and improve the mobility of the muscles. Fascia is a thin, web-like tissue that covers and connects all of the structures in the body, including muscles, bones, nerves, and organs. It helps to transmit force throughout the body and provides support and stability. However, fascia can also become tight and restricted, which can lead to pain and decreased range of motion. The spiky balls apply pressure to the fascia, which can help to release tension and improve the mobility of the muscles. Some of the benefits of using spiky massage balls for myofascial release are, they can: help to relieve muscle tension and pain. improve range of motion. reduce inflammation. improve circulation. help to relax the mind and body. Myofascial release therapy can be used to treat a variety of conditions, including: Muscle pain: Myofascial release can help to relieve muscle pain by releasing tension in the fascia. Headaches: Myofascial release can help to relieve headaches by releasing tension in the muscles of the neck and shoulders. Back pain: Myofascial release can help to relieve back pain by releasing tension in the muscles of the back and spine. Joint pain: Myofascial release can help to relieve joint pain by releasing tension in the muscles that surround the joint. Fibromyalgia: Myofascial release can help to relieve the pain and stiffness associated with fibromyalgia. Hip impingement, also known as femoroacetabular impingement (FAI), occurs when the bones of the hip joint are abnormally shaped, causing them to rub against each other. This friction can lead to pain and damage over time. 🔍 Common Causes: Abnormal bone growth (Cam or Pincer deformity) Hip joint deformities High-impact activities or sports Repetitive hip movements 😣 Key Symptoms: Deep groin pain, especially after activity Limited range of motion Stiffness in the hip Sharp pain during twisting or squatting 💪 The Role of Physiotherapy: Physiotherapy can play a crucial role in managing hip impingement. Targeted exercises help to strengthen the muscles around the hip, improve flexibility, and enhance the range of motion.  With a personalised physiotherapy plan, many people experience significant reductions in pain and improvements in their ability to move without discomfort. That was in 2021/ early 2022. - I was previously diagnosed with fibromyalgia in 2019. The symptoms I had brought up:     * joint pains    * memory and cognitive issues    * bladder control issues     * extreme fatigue    * weight gain and overeating (out of control)    * I also started spending and drinking too much    * Issues with my voice (I’m a singer) - I was diagnosed with fibromyalgia - historically diagnosed with Major Depressive Disorder (with EUPD traits) - it’s a whole other post but I’m undiagnosed ADHD (awaiting diagnostic assessment) - doctors kept saying I was “too young” despite maternal history of menopause at 45 - doctors would blame depression, fibro, stress, obesity, anaemia and vit D deficiency for how I was feeling - I was even at one point sent for an urgent cancer referral! Hypermobility and fibromyalgia are two distinct but sometimes interconnected medical conditions that affect the musculoskeletal system. Hypermobility refers to an increased range of motion in the joints beyond the normal range, often due to the laxity of connective tissues. This condition is commonly seen in conditions such as Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome. People with hypermobility may experience joint pain, frequent dislocations, and a higher incidence of soft tissue injuries. On the other hand, fibromyalgia is a chronic condition characterized by widespread musculoskeletal pain, fatigue, and tenderness in localized areas. Interestingly, there is a notable overlap between the two conditions; individuals with hypermobility are more likely to develop fibromyalgia. This may be due to the constant strain and micro-injuries in hypermobile joints, which can contribute to chronic pain syndromes. It's pain awareness month, Crohn's and Colitis do not just affect the gut, they can cause problems in other parts of the body, called extraintestinal manifestations or EIMs. Joint problems are one of the most common types of EIM related to Crohn’s or Colitis. Recent studies have found that up to 46 in every 100 people with Crohn’s or Colitis may experience joint problems. Key facts: 🦵Joint problems can include joint pain and swelling in the joints in your back, hands, feet, arms and legs. 🦵Spondyloarthritis is a group of inflammatory arthritis conditions. This means your immune system has caused damage in your joints. Having Crohn's or Colitis can increase your risk of developing spondyloarthritis. 🦵Joint problems can come and go. For some people they get worse when your Crohn’s or Colitis is worse. For others, you may have a flare-up of arthritis symptoms with no gut symptoms. 🦵If left untreated, some arthritis conditions can lead to permanent damage. Speak to your GP or IBD team if you have pain, swelling or stiffness in your joints. 🦵Medicine treatments, exercise and physiotherapy can all be helpful in managing joint problems. If you take HRT to help with symptoms of perimenopause and menopause then oestrogen is one of the hormones you will be given. This is the one that will help to relieve your symptoms.  It can be taken through the skin , where it is absorbed into the bloodstream, as a gel, as a patch stuck to the skin, or as a spray sprayed onto the skin. It can also be taken as an oral tablet.  If you have a uterus  / womb then you will also be advised to take a progestogen. Some people without a womb are advised to take a progestogen.  The doses of oestrogen and progestogen must balance . Please do not adjust the dose of your HRT without speaking to your doctor .  If you have any concerns about your HRT, please speak with your doctor .  This video is for guidance only , please follow the advice of your healthcare provider. What a cruel disease 😢 please take time to read 👇🏻 Ryan was diagnosed with Rheumatoid and Psoriatic arthritis 8 years ago. He had a major flare up at the age of 32 resulting in him being unable to walk as it affected his knees and feet.  Arthritis is an autoimmune disease, your immune system attacks your joints leaving the person in unimaginable pain and joint deformity but can also attack your organs  For 8 years until recently Ryan has been on methotrexate tablets which kills his immune system but has made him really sick and loose his hair but kept the arthritis at bay.  Then two months ago he had a major flare up with the arthritis spreading to his spine and hips. The pain was so bad we had to rush him to hospital he was unable to walk and the drs struggled to get his pain under control. To watch the person you love in so much pain was heartbreaking.  We had to wait 4 weeks but he’s now been given a new biological medication which is administered by a needle each week. Already after a week we have noticed a major difference he is able to walk better. We are hoping this is the start and he can start building his strength back up.  This medication is killing his immune system we have to be careful of bringing bugs in the house and keeping things clean but we are taking one step at a time and hoping to keep the arthritis at bay.  This awful disease affects so many people especially young people and we’ve found it’s not spoken about enough and people just don’t understand its impact. Thank you to all of those that have messaged me over the past few months to offer advice and we would like to do more to raise awareness and help those struggling  Ryan & Fay x  #arthritis #rhumatoidarthritis #psoriaticarthritis #autoimunedisease #raisingawareness #jointpain

Do your joints let you know when damp rainy weather is coming without you needing to see the forecast?  According to a study done by Harvard Medical School’s Professor Robert Jamison, 67.9% of people surveyed felt the same. He concluded that the increased pain may be due to a change in barometric pressure (atmospheric pressure), which normally pushes against the body from the outside. When the weather worsens, the barometric pressure falls, causing tissues in the body to expand and push on the nerve endings that signal pain. The good news is that Myofascial Release treatment can help to reduce the restrictions around your joints, giving more space for expansion without pushing on the nerve endings.
